thread:
Luis: hi folks, i'm Luis, joining eng-runtime. first build from source succeeded but when running the small integration smoke I see runtime loader warnings and a crash: 

[rtld] warning: cannot open shared object file: libcusparse.so.11: No such file or directory
OSError: Failed to load extension: /workspace/build/libinfruntime.so: undefined symbol: cusparseCreateCsr

anyone seen this day-0? i'm using a devcontainer that includes CUDA 12 toolkit folders under /usr/local/cuda but i'm not sure the right way to surface host driver libs to the runtime container.

Anika: welcome Luis! short answer: toolkit headers vs driver libs mismatch. The build can link against the toolkit copy, but at runtime the loader needs the host's driver-provided libs (libcuda, libcublas, libcusstuff). In containers we usually mount the host driver dir and set RUNPATH or LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Which base image are you using?

Luis: using ghcr.io/redwood/infr-dev:cuda12 as the devcontainer base. ldd build/libinfruntime.so shows libcublas.so.12 => /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublas.so.12 and libcusparse.so.11 => not found. readelf -d shows RUNPATH: [$ORIGIN/../lib:/usr/local/lib] 

Ravi: if libcusparse resolves to not found, that means the driver variant isn't present inside the container. Two approaches: 1) use nvidia-container-toolkit + --gpus to mount host libs automatically, or 2) bind-mount host lib dir into container and update LD_LIBRARY_PATH. For devcontainers we prefer a helper script that adds /host-drivers to LD_LIBRARY_PATH at container start.

Luis: i tried mounting /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu to /host-drivers and export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-drivers before running tests, but the Python process still crashed with undefined symbol. Could this be version mismatch?

Anika: yes, likely. Check sonames and symbol versions: run `objdump -p /host-drivers/libcusparse.so | grep SONAME` and `nm -D /host-drivers/libcusparse.so | grep cusparseCreateCsr`. If the symbol isn't present, the host driver is too old/new relative to the toolkit your build used. Also check `strings /host-drivers/libcuda.so | grep 'Driver Version'` or `nvidia-smi` on host.

Luis: host `nvidia-smi` shows Driver Version: 525.60, CUDA Version: 12.1. The toolkit in the container is 12.2. Is that enough to cause missing symbols?

Ravi: sometimes minor mismatch is OK, but cusparse API additions can change across minor versions. Best fix: build against the same toolkit version you will run against, or use the host's headers to build (bind-mount /usr/include/cuda). For day-0 dev, we usually pin the devcontainer toolkit to match the host driver, or use a binary-compatible shim: set LD_LIBRARY_PATH so runtime picks host libs first.

Anika: additional tip: if you can't change build, you can patch the built .so RUNPATH to include /host-drivers with patchelf so loader finds host libs before packaged ones: `patchelf --set-rpath '$ORIGIN/../lib:/host-drivers:/usr/local/lib' build/libinfruntime.so`. But patchelf is a last resort.

Luis: patchelf trick + host mount fixed the smoke tests locally. For CI, should we add a preflight to assert host libs are present or to fail early if toolkit libs exist in runtime image?

ci-bot: CI suggestion: add a job step that runs inside the runtime image and executes `python -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')"` and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader` — fail with clear message if either fails. We also keep a small `ci/runtime-check.sh` in repo.

Ravi: great, Luis—push the fix to your branch and ping me if CI complains. Welcome aboard :wave:
